acceptance: Reproduce the crash or bound its rate over repeated SF1 runs on the Linux runner image
Name the native component and operation that faults (faulthandler or core dump)
Fix or pin around the cause so the cell passes repeatedly without retry; no cell pruning or gate loosening
context:
Raised to high 2026-11-11 (owner): a product-class crash in a gated cell, seen in one of five executions of that cell; run 42718296767 was turned green by a manual partial rerun, which also hid the crash from per-cell history (all rows record run_attempt 2).

Follow-up landed 2026-11-11: PR #4087 (merge 3a8ddae5) makes release evidence reuse refuse a trunk UAT run whose latest attempt re-ran only some required jobs (each job's started_at is compared with the attempt's run_started_at; for run 42718296767 only 'UAT stage 1 pandas-df', gate and record started after attempt 2's 01:53:47Z start). trunk_uat.py record now attributes each shard's cells to the attempt that produced them and marks partial_rerun/carried_over_shards, so a crash fixed by rerun stays visible in history.

Revalidated 2026-11-11 (develop c7b75c80bc): still required, text accurate. No recurrence since the one crash: trunk UAT scheduled runs 42789483182 (2026-11-10, ce39d7680) and 42990393684 (2026-11-11, beab5557e) both concluded success on attempt 1 (no rerun), with the pandas-df shard in the matrix (trunk-uat.yml:124, release-gate-01 config). That is three consecutive green full runs after the crash (42718296767 attempt 2 included), so the observed rate is 1 failure in ~6 executions of the cell, still with no named native component and no faulthandler/core evidence. PR #4087 (3a8ddae5) keeps such a crash visible in history if it recurs. Remaining scope is unchanged: bound the rate and capture faulthandler/core output on the Linux runner image. I only had run-level conclusions for the two scheduled runs (the jobs API returned 502), not per-cell rows.

2026-11-12: recurrence on a different platform. Trunk UAT 43229090202 (source 01a15152) stage1 duckdb: write_primitives SF1 aborted with 'malloc(): unsorted double linked list corrupted' (exit 134, peak RSS 1.35 GiB, no traceback); the other 55 DuckDB cells passed. No DuckDB or uv.lock change since the last passing run. So the native crash is in the shared write_primitives SF1 path, not pandas-specific. Owner: investigate in parallel with the 0.5.1 release; if the next trunk UAT crashes again, escalate before tagging.

2026-11-12 investigation: 5 of 5 duckdb write_primitives SF1 runs clean on aarch64 glibc 2.39 (Apple container VM, duckdb 1.5.5, pyarrow 24.0.0, pandas 3.0.5) with MALLOC_CHECK_=3 and faulthandler; this bounds the local rate below about 45% only. No BenchBox threading or connection sharing on the path. Suspects: DuckDB ART/primary-key inserts on a file-backed database (duckdb#23046, open, reported on 1.5.0) or a pyarrow/DuckDB allocator interaction (Arrow fetch mode). Next: capture MALLOC_CHECK_/faulthandler/core dump in the CI stage1 job (touches guarded UAT paths, so do it outside a release evidence window), and bisect on x86_64 with enable_primary_keys=False and fetch_mode=rows.
description: Trunk UAT run https://github.com/BenchBox-dev/BenchBox/actions/runs/42718296767 attempt 1 (develop 52615914002012e24405b77b830dc98d35ba50e9) failed pandas-df write_primitives SF1 with exit 139 (SIGSEGV) about 35 s in, after loading the TPC-H tables twice and before any Python traceback; the in-harness diagnostic rerun timed out (exit 124). Attempt 2 of the same job passed. The same cell passed in run 42536258036, and the commits between those sources do not touch pandas, write_primitives or uv.lock, so the crash is native and intermittent.
